verdict.label: not_replicated
verdict.rationale: Both abstracts examine the effect of SGLT2 inhibitors on triglycerides as a within-group change from baseline. Side A (PMID 37329705) reports that triglycerides 'significantly decreased' in the SGLT2i group after six months of therapy (sentence 6), a directional effect with explicit significance wording. Side B (PMID 30503071) explicitly reports a substantive no-difference conclusion for the same outcome: 'no differences were observed for total cholesterol, triglycerides or cLDL' after SGLT2 inhibitor treatment in insulin-treated T2D patients (sentence 8). The exposures (SGLT2 inhibitors), outcome (triglycerides), and contrast type (within-group change from baseline) are sufficiently similar for comparison, and the extractions on both sides accurately reflect their sources. Because one source reports a significant decrease and the other explicitly reports no difference for triglycerides, the pair falls into the not_replicated branch; no text-supported contextual difference is needed to explain this abstract-level finding, so the factor is none.

source_evidence.quote: Body mass index, triglycerides, aspartate aminotransferase, uric acid, E/E', deceleration time and systolic pressure in the pulmonary artery significantly decreased, while stroke volume, indexed stroke volume, high-density lipoprotein, hematocrit and hemoglobin significantly increased in the group on SGLT2i.
A global cHDL increase was noted after treatment, while no differences were observed for total cholesterol, triglycerides or cLDL.

diagnostics.notes: Side A claim correctly extracted as a significant within-group decrease in triglycerides in the SGLT2i group; side B claim correctly extracted as an explicit no-difference assertion for triglycerides.
